correctness.rationale: Verified the actual pinned RESULT.md, verify.py, verification output and all eight pinned tree blob IDs. From the two nonparallel line equations, X_σ(q),Y_σ(q) are affine in q, with ell1(center)=q√3563201 and ell2(center)=σq√6112121. With Q=diag(20,-5,1) and circle matrix C, det(Q+λC)=−q²λ³+(1+20X²−5Y²−15q²)λ²+(15−100(X²+Y²−q²))λ−100. The cubic discriminant is a degree-eight polynomial in q on both branches. Independent rational-interval arithmetic encloses √3563201 and √6112121 using 65-decimal integer square-root brackets and certifies eight disjoint real sign-change intervals for σ=+ and six for σ=−; in the latter branch a conjugate pair is isolated in disjoint nonreal disks by exact rational coefficient-bound Rouché inequalities. Thus the eight polynomial roots on each branch are simple and exhaust its complex roots; q=0 excluded. Every real eliminant root corresponds to real Euclidean tangency, not merely a formal necessary condition: the repeated root of a real cubic pencil is real; the symmetric pencil at it has rank exactly two because X and Y are nonzero throughout all certified root brackets; the determinant derivative then forces its real one-dimensional kernel vector onto both conics with proportional gradients, and the real circle has no projective real point at infinity. Distinct nonzero q and opposite signs yield distinct centers/circles. Consequently there are exactly 8+6 real circles without relying exclusively on the source's reported 14. The interval and Rouché certificates use integer/rational operations; independent high-precision Sturm counts reproduce 8,6 as corroboration. These are exhaustive degree-eight root arguments, not finite q sampling.
